topic: Status of yet in a positive protasis
claim: Explaining why unless can’t replace if not in [55iii] I’m cancelling the order if the goods aren’t ready yet, CGEL says that yet “is not compatible with the other component” of an unless conditional, and stars the positive version: “∗If the goods are ready yet I’m not cancelling the order.”
evidence_summary: Page 745 accepts yet in a positive if protasis without a mark: [23ib] I’ll be surprised if they are here yet. It marks comparable clashes of orientation with ?, not ∗: [24ii] ?If you were at all worried about the project, why didn’t you let me know?, where at all “is here infelicitous”, and [24iii] ?If you improve your performance at all, we give you a bonus. Ch. 9, p. 838: “A clause embedded as complement of if generally allows NPIs”.
finding: Medium-low confidence. Either mark the p. 756 example ? or say why yet is worse here than at all in [24]. The defence that yet is a stronger negative polarity item than at all (Ch. 9, p. 823, “Varying strength of the restrictions”) partly works.
inference: Is yet in a positive protasis ungrammatical or infelicitous?

evidence.passage: §14.3, p. 756. “∗If the goods are ready yet I’m not cancelling the order”
evidence.establishes: The chapter marks comparable polarity clashes in conditional protases with ? or with no mark.
